text:
**You need about 300 to 350 W of solar panels to refill a 1,000 Wh power station from empty in one day of decent sun.** A 200 W panel will do it in about a day and a half.

**The formula:** panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle and charging losses, because panels rarely deliver their rated watts ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).

**Panel watts for a full recharge in one day** ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)):

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts |
|---|---|
| 3 | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 | ~230 W |

Winter in northern states is the worst case, at about 2 peak sun hours. That takes roughly 700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**If you'd rather use a smaller panel:**
- A 200 W panel at 4.5 peak sun hours gives about 630 Wh a day, so roughly 1.5 days to refill ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).
- A 400 W panel gives about 1,260 Wh a day, so it refills in under a day ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A quick rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5, which gives about 200 W for a day and a half.

**Before you buy:**
- **Input limit:** Your station caps how many solar watts it accepts. A 200 W cap means extra panels add nothing.
- **Voltage:** Panels wired in series add voltage. Keep the combined open-circuit voltage inside the station's input window, or you risk damaging it.
- **Running loads:** If you use the station while it charges, subtract that draw from the solar input, and recharging takes longer.
